structure: Part 16, Address book: all 9 traces of address-book.fit.spec.js, every one opened and mined (actions, accessibility/innerText and outerHTML of main, error summaries, notification banners and the network log). All passed with no recorded errors; validation copy is rendered error state. Traces: (1) address book list › categories, pagination and filters (94 actions: list default category, Next to page 2, the three other category tabs, then the Filter addresses disclosure and a live search for 'Ballymore'); (2) add › choose an address type (page plus the empty-submit error); (3) add › origin or consignor: an address entered by hand with its uses (type, manual-entry lookup page, empty-submit errors, filled save, list with success banner); (4) add › destination, consignee or importer: a UK address found by search (type, UK search lookup page, empty-submit errors, type-ahead pick that fills the fields and reveals the uses); (5) add › branch: the branch address use (UK lookup page with the single Branch address use); (6) add › transporter: hands over to the add-a-transporter pages (type then /transporter/add, Choose a transporter type); (7) add › the usage step is only reachable with an address pending (GET /address-book/add/usage redirects to /address-book/add); (8) an address book entry › view, edit and save (view summary, edit form, blank-name error, save to the list with an updated banner); (9) an address book entry › delete: confirm, then the list says it was deleted. Pages in order: Address book list (/design-release-2.1/address-book, ?category=origin-and-consignor|destination-consignee-importer|transporter|branch, &page=N) -> Choose an address type (/address-book/add) -> either Add address and contact details (/address-book/add/lookup; manual-entry form for Origin or Consignor, UK address search for Destination/Consignee/Importer and Branch) -> back to the list with a success banner, or, for Transporter, Choose a transporter type (/transporter/add, owned by the transport part). Entry pages: view (/address-book/<slug>) -> edit (/address-book/<slug>/edit) or delete confirmation (/address-book/<slug>/delete) -> list with a success banner. Conditional: the lookup page layout and the address uses depend on the chosen type; the uses fieldset on the UK search layout appears only once an address is picked; the usage route (/address-book/add/usage) only renders with an address pending and was never rendered. Refs cite trace zips by their file name under sources/traces-prototype and the action id snapshotted. The spec file was read for test titles only.

claims.quote: Confirm that you want to delete this address.

claims.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
The delete page has a red warning button 'Yes, delete' that submits the deletion, beside a 'No, cancel' link back to the entry page.
The delete page's Back link returns to the entry page.
Confirming the deletion returns to the address book list with a success banner titled 'Success' with '<name> address deleted', the name in sentence case.
claims.quote: Success / Green valley farm address deleted

claims.statement: A deleted address is removed from the list: the Origin and Consignor count drops from 23 to 22 and the list starts at Valea Mare Farm.
claims.note: Only the Place of origin entry was deleted; whether the same organisation's Consignor entry is affected is not shown.

claims.statement: Every address book page is rendered by the prototype server and every change is a plain form post followed by a redirect; no separate address book API is called and the entries live in the user's session.
claims.note: Inferred from the network logs of all nine traces: only page GETs and form POSTs to the prototype on localhost:3010, plus the kit's dev socket. Each trace starts with a fresh seed (23 origin entries), so the state is per session. The rebuild needs a real address book store.

claims.statement: The add-address, entry and delete pages use GOV.UK components (caption, heading, inputs, select, checkboxes, summary list, buttons, button group, error summary, notification banner) with custom wrapper classes; the choose-type page reuses a class from the reason-for-import radios.
claims.note: The custom pieces are layout wrappers, the type-ahead address search, and custom heading classes on the list, choose-type and edit pages.

claims.statement: No trace renders the separate address uses step at /address-book/add/usage, so what it asks and when it appears is not shown.
claims.note: In every trace the uses are asked on the add-address page itself.

claims.statement: No trace completes saving a Destination, Consignee or Importer or a Branch address, so the save, the uses validation and the banner for those types are not shown.
No trace opens the 'Enter address manually' route on the UK search layout, or searches with no matching address.
No trace changes the Type filter, searches with no match on the list, or visits page 3, so filtering by type, an empty-results message and the last page are not shown.
No trace opens, edits or deletes a Transporter, Destination or Branch entry, so their entry pages (and whether a transporter shows its approval number and type) are not shown.
No trace drives format validation of email address, phone number or postcode, or a length limit on any field; only blank-field messages are shown.
No trace uses the edit page's 'Cancel' button, the delete page's 'No, cancel' link or the add page's 'Cancel and return to address book' link, so where they land is only known from their hrefs.
